Goats give milk 10 months a year and they need to have kids every year to produce. Furthermore, not all goats give tasty milk. Pygmy goat milk for example tastes terrible. The best goat milk I've heard is from Nigerian dwarf goats. It has a high fat concentration and almost no sugar. It's also important to separate males from females while they're sleeping. Otherwise, the females will release hormones which will give a foul taste to the milk.

They don't really need any special diet provided the land they graze on isn't mineral deficient. if the land hasn't been used for agriculture before then it's probably safe to say it's ok. Giving them a mineral salt lick won't hurt though. They're actually pretty picky eaters and will selectively eat the most nutritious vegetation, but are also hardy and can eat just about anything.
